issues.legal_issue: A property transfer can be declared void under the senior-citizen transfer remedy only when it was made subject to the transferee providing basic amenities and physical needs, and the transferee refuses or fails to provide them; the remedy covers transfers by release as well as by gift.
material_facts: A senior citizen sought cancellation of a registered release deed transferring property to her daughters.
Neither the petition nor the response alleged that the release deed was subject to a condition requiring the daughters to provide basic amenities and physical needs.
No oral evidence was adduced to establish such a condition.
The tribunal declared the release deed void after finding that the children were unwilling to care for the senior citizen, and the High Court affirmed that order.
issues.conclusion: The required conditions for declaring the transfer void were not satisfied. The appeal was allowed, the tribunal and High Court orders were set aside, and the petition seeking cancellation of the transfer was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 23(1) of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 covers transfers by gift or otherwise, including releases, but requires both that the transfer be made subject to the transferee providing the transferor’s basic amenities and physical needs and that the transferee refuse or fail to provide them. Only when both conditions are satisfied is the transfer deemed to have been made by fraud, coercion or undue influence and made voidable at the transferor’s option. The required condition must be established before the Maintenance Tribunal. Sections 7 and 8 provide for the Tribunal and its inquiry procedure. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.senior_citizen_transfer_challenge: A senior citizen sought before a maintenance tribunal to have a property transfer declared void.
predicates.transfer_condition_not_established: The transferor did not plead or establish that the transferee was required under the transfer to provide the transferor’s basic amenities and physical needs.

issues.definition: When a senior citizen seeks to have a property transfer declared void and the required care condition was not established, the transfer cannot be declared void under that remedy.
